name: ION-16693 Visibility Lambda OWASP (jna-jpms HIGH)
description: Address jna-jpms 5.14.0 HIGH OWASP finding on the four visibility lambda deployment packages (s3-archiver, error-email, pending-start, outbound-poller). Follow-up to the 2026-08-31 visibility OWASP refactor (commons 1.0.33-SNAPSHOT). Branch feature/ION-16693-vis-lambda-owasp-fix.

entries.summary: Root cause: jna-jpms 5.14.0 HIGH is a dependency-check FALSE POSITIVE (CPE sun:java_se, Low confidence); arrives via cloud-sdk-api -> dropwizard-core 5.0.2 -> jetty-setuid-jna 2.0.3; visible only in lambdas because they ship an exploded lib/ ZIP instead of a shaded uber-jar
entries.detail:
OWASP summary-table extraction from the 4 Jenkins CI reports (26.09.002) shows an IDENTICAL set of 3 HIGH rows in all four lambdas:

| Dependency | Highest Sev | CVE count | CPE confidence | CPE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| jackson-databind-2.22.0.jar | HIGH | 5 | Highest | cpe:2.3:a:fasterxml:jackson-databind:2.22.0 |
| jna-jpms-5.14.0.jar | HIGH | 9 | **Low** | cpe:2.3:a:**sun:java_se**:5.14.0 |
| jsoup-1.17.2.jar | HIGH | 2 | Highest | cpe:2.3:a:jsoup:jsoup@1.17.2 |

jackson-databind + jsoup are the two HIGHs the user is taking a release exception for (also present in other modules at commons 1.0.33-SNAPSHOT). In scope for this session: jna-jpms only.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE jna-jpms FINDING = FALSE POSITIVE CPE MATCH.
dependency-check's CPE analyzer mapped net.java.dev.jna:jna-jpms 5.14.0 onto `cpe:2.3:a:sun:java_se:5.14.0` (Oracle/Sun Java SE) at **Low** confidence, because the jar's package namespace is `com/sun/jna/**` and it embeds native `jnidispatch.dll` / `.so` / `.dylib` binaries whose only evidence is "Vendor=jnidispatch (file name), Product=jnidispatch (file name)". The 9 CVEs are Oracle Java SE CVEs, not JNA CVEs. Confirmed from the report:
  jna-jpms-5.14.0.jar cpe:2.3:a:sun:java_se:5.14.0 pkg:maven/net.java.dev.jna/jna-jpms@5.14.0 HIGH 9 Low 54
  ...matched "cpe:2.3:a:sun:java_se:*:14:*" versions up to (including) 6

DEPENDENCY ORIGIN (mvn dependency:tree, visibility-s3-archiver):
  com.inttra.mercury:visibility-s3-archiver:jar:1.0
  \- com.inttra.mercury:cloud-sdk-api:jar:1.0.33-SNAPSHOT:compile
     \- io.dropwizard:dropwizard-core:jar:5.0.2:compile
        \- org.eclipse.jetty.toolchain.setuid:jetty-setuid-jna:jar:2.0.3:compile
           \- net.java.dev.jna:jna-jpms:jar:5.14.0:compile
dropwizard-core 5.0.2 declares jetty-setuid-jna as a direct compile dependency (dropwizard-core-5.0.2.pom line 167-169; version property jetty-setuid-jna.version=2.0.3 in dropwizard-dependencies-5.0.2.pom).

WHY ONLY THE LAMBDAS:
The 4 lambda modules package via maven-assembly-plugin src/assembly/deployment_package.xml -> a ZIP with a `lib/` dependencySet, i.e. every runtime dependency stays a SEPARATE jar file that dependency-check unpacks and scans as its own dependency node (and it recurses into the jar to find the jnidispatch native libs). The other visibility modules ship a maven-shade uber-jar, where JNA's classes are merged into one artifact, so no standalone `jna-jpms-5.14.0.jar` node is ever created and the sun:java_se CPE is never assigned. Verified: Visibility-26.09.005-OWASP.html (shaded app) has 0 occurrences of "jna-jpms"; all four lambda reports have 53 each.

RUNTIME REACHABILITY:
`io.dropwizard.core.server.AbstractServerFactory` is the ONLY dropwizard-core class referencing org.eclipse.jetty.setuid (verified by extracting dropwizard-core-5.0.2.jar and scanning every .class). Its `buildServer(LifecycleEnvironment, ThreadPool)` UNCONDITIONALLY calls `buildSetUIDListener()` -> `new org.eclipse.jetty.setuid.SetUIDListener()`. So a reactor-wide exclusion would break every Dropwizard service in visibility. The 4 lambdas are AWS RequestHandler implementations and contain ZERO references to io.dropwizard / jetty / Configuration (grep over all 4 src trees = no matches), so they never build a Jetty Server.

entries.summary: Explained local-vs-Jenkins OWASP discrepancy: (1) jna FP is hidden locally by dependency-check's hosted publishedSuppressions.xml (upstream declares sun:java_se on maven artifacts an FP); Jenkins agent lacks that file. (2) Jenkins' 490 vs local 240 dep count = it scans exploded lib/ AND the zip, cataloguing all 221 jars twice. Both proven by controlled experiment; same DC 13.0.0 both sides.
entries.detail:
User asked why their local run
  dependency-check --project visibility-ob-poller --scan .\visibility-outbound-poller-1.0-deployment_package.zip --out owasp --suppression ..\suppressions.xml --nvdApiKey $env:NVD_API_KEY
(run BEFORE the fix) showed jackson-databind + jsoup HIGH but NOT jna-jpms, while Jenkins showed all three and ~2x the dependency count.

ANSWER: the command was correct. Two INDEPENDENT differences, both proven by controlled experiment.

(1) THE jna FALSE POSITIVE IS SUPPRESSED LOCALLY BY THE HOSTED SUPPRESSION FILE.
Both sides run dependency-check 13.0.0 (Jenkins HTML footer literally states "dependency-check version : 13.0.0"), so it is NOT a version gap.
dependency-check auto-downloads <data>/publishedSuppressions.xml. That file (local copy dated 2026-09-01) contains an upstream base rule:
    <suppress base="true">
      <notes>FP per issue #8257, #8701, #8718, #8719, #8720, #8721, #8722, #8723</notes>
      <packageUrl regex="true">^pkg:maven/.*@.*$</packageUrl>
      <cpe regex="true">cpe:/a:oracle:java_se(:.*)?$</cpe>
      <cpe regex="true">cpe:/a:sun:java_se(:.*)?$</cpe>
    </suppress>
i.e. upstream itself declares sun/oracle:java_se on a Maven artifact to be a false positive. The dev workstation has internet + --nvdApiKey so it has the file; the Jenkins agent evidently does not (no egress to the hosted-suppressions URL), so the FP surfaces there.

IMPORTANT SUBTLETY: passing --disableHostedSuppressions is NOT enough to reproduce Jenkins - an already-downloaded publishedSuppressions.xml is still applied. Had to clone the data dir and delete the file:
    Copy-Item C:\dependency-check\dependency-check-current\data\* $env:TEMP\dc-data-nosupp -Recurse
    Remove-Item $env:TEMP\dc-data-nosupp\publishedSuppressions.xml*
    dependency-check.bat --scan <jna-jpms-5.14.0.jar> --data $env:TEMP\dc-data-nosupp --noupdate --disableHostedSuppressions
RESULT - reproduces Jenkins exactly:
    CPE: cpe:2.3:a:sun:java_se:5.14.0:*:*:*:*:*:*:*  | confidence: LOW
    vulnerabilities: 9  -> {HIGH: 4, MEDIUM: 5}
    CVE-2009-2476/2689/2475/2716 (HIGH) + CVE-2009-2676/2717/2690/2719/2720 (MEDIUM)
All nine are 2009 Sun Java SE CVEs, against a JNA library released in 2024 - conclusive false positive.
With the file present: 0 vulnerabilities and vulnerabilityIds is EMPTY (the CPE itself is stripped).

(2) THE ~2x DEPENDENCY COUNT IS JENKINS SCANNING THE PACKAGE TWICE.
Jenkins reports "Dependencies Scanned : 490" (outbound-poller) / 492 (s3-archiver); local zip scan reports 240/241.
Parsing the Jenkins report's file paths shows the scanned workspace contains BOTH the exploded lib/ AND the .zip:
    <ws>/VisibilityOutboundPoller-26.09.002-<ts>/lib/<jar>            -> 221 distinct jars
    <ws>/VisibilityOutboundPoller-26.09.002-<ts>/<pkg>.zip/lib/<jar>  -> the SAME 221 jars
    jars appearing in both forms: 221 (100%)
So every jar is catalogued twice (221 x 2 = 442, plus native .dll/.so entries and the zip itself = 490). The 206 "Related Dependencies" blocks in the report are dependency-check merging those pairs. 221 also exactly matches the pre-fix lib/ jar count reconstructed locally.
A/B control (same content scanned as zip-only vs as an exploded dir) gave IDENTICAL results locally - 206 dependency entries either way - so the scan LAYOUT does not change findings, only the duplicate cataloguing inflates the count.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX: a suppressions.xml entry would also have silenced this, but removing the dependency is strictly better - the artifact is gone from the package, so the finding cannot recur regardless of scanner configuration, and the dead jar (plus its bundled Windows/macOS/Linux native libs) leaves the deployment ZIP.
RECOMMENDATION for the platform/CI team: give the Jenkins agent access to the hosted suppression list (or commit a copy and pass --suppression), otherwise every known upstream FP will keep appearing only in CI.

entries.detail:
Final state of the visibility-lambda OWASP fix.

COMMIT: 9793f14a48 on branch feature/ION-16693-vis-lambda-owasp-fix
  4 files changed, +77/-1 (poms only)
  - visibility/visibility-s3-archiver/pom.xml   : exclude jetty-setuid-jna on cloud-sdk-api, cloud-sdk-aws, visibility-commons; log4j-core 2.23.1 -> ${log4j.version} (2.25.5)
  - visibility/visibility-pending-start/pom.xml : exclude jetty-setuid-jna (x3 deps)
  - visibility/visibility-outbound-poller/pom.xml : exclude jetty-setuid-jna (x3 deps)
  - visibility/visibility-error-email/pom.xml   : exclude jetty-setuid-jna on visibility-commons (its only mercury dep)

DOC: visibility/docs/2026-09-01-visibility-lambda-owasp.md
  NOTE FOR FUTURE SESSIONS - repo doc convention is a DATE-PREFIXED FILENAME directly
  under <module>/docs/, i.e. docs/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md. Do NOT create a docs/<date>/ folder.
  Corrected by the user this session. Also note **/docs/ is gitignored (.gitignore:110),
  so module docs are local-only and are never part of the commit.
  10 sections: summary; origin of jna-jpms; why lambda-only; false-positive proof;
  local-vs-Jenkins scan discrepancy; the fix; verification; commands used (16 numbered
  commands with syntax + explanation); files changed; residual risk.

ROOT CAUSE RECAP:
  dropwizard-core 5.0.2 declares org.eclipse.jetty.toolchain.setuid:jetty-setuid-jna:2.0.3
  directly, which pulls net.java.dev.jna:jna-jpms:5.14.0. Lambda-only because the 4 lambdas
  run maven-assembly-plugin (deployment_package.xml keeps each dependency as its own jar in
  lib/) while the other 7 modules ship a shaded uber-jar, so DC never sees a standalone
  jna-jpms jar there.

FALSE POSITIVE: DC matched jna-jpms to cpe:2.3:a:sun:java_se:5.14.0 at LOW confidence
  (com/sun/jna/** namespace + jnidispatch native evidence). All 9 CVEs are 2009 Sun Java SE
  JRE bugs. Upstream DC suppresses this in its hosted publishedSuppressions.xml.

SAFETY: AbstractServerFactory is the only dropwizard-core class referencing
  org/eclipse/jetty/setuid, and buildServer() calls buildSetUIDListener() UNCONDITIONALLY
  (javap -c verified) -> the exclusion MUST stay lambda-only, never reactor-wide.

VERIFICATION: mvn -o clean verify BUILD SUCCESS across all 12 visibility modules (unit +
  failsafe/DynamoDB ITs); 0 jna/setuid jars in all 4 ZIPs (220/219/219/219 lib jars); all 4
  handlers boot from their actual deployment ZIPs via Class.forName(initialize=true) + no-arg
  ctor, exit 0, reaching app code and stopping only at env-var validation; constant-pool scan
  of ~220 jars per lambda shows no reachable setuid ref; DC re-scan shows 0 HIGH and no jna
  artifact; all 7 non-lambda modules still resolve jetty-setuid-jna:2.0.3 unchanged.

ALSO FIXED (pre-existing, unrelated): VisibilityS3ArchiverIT was failing with
  NoSuchMethodError ServiceLoaderUtil.loadServices - s3-archiver was the only module
  hardcoding log4j-core 2.23.1 against log4j-api 2.25.5. Missed yesterday because
  verification used `mvn package`, which does not run failsafe. Lesson: use `mvn verify`.

OUT OF SCOPE (agreed release exception, code freeze): jackson-databind-2.22.0 and
  jsoup-1.17.2 HIGHs - both jars still ship unchanged, also present in other modules on
  commons 1.0.33-SNAPSHOT.

OPEN ITEM FOR CI/PLATFORM: give the Jenkins agent egress to DC's hosted suppression URL, or
  commit publishedSuppressions.xml and pass --suppression. Otherwise every upstream-known FP
  will keep surfacing in CI only. Captured in section 5.3 of the doc.

EXPECTED NEXT JENKINS SCAN: 2 HIGH instead of 3, jna-jpms row gone, ~2 fewer jars per package.

entries.summary: ION-16693 follow-ups: commons 1.0.27 was a -pl-without-am artifact; s3-archiver IT never runs in CI; jsoup/jackson HIGHs are OSS-Index-only and DC13 needs a token; 12.2.2 data copy harmless; suppression-rename reproduces the jna HIGH exactly
entries.detail:
Five follow-up questions from the user, all investigated with controlled experiments. Doc updated
(visibility/docs/2026-09-01-visibility-lambda-owasp.md, now 11 sections). No code change needed;
commit 9793f14a48 stands.

--- Q1: why did error-email show commons 1.0.27-SNAPSHOT? ---
IT WAS A PROBE ARTIFACT, NOT REALITY. My probe was `mvn -o dependency:tree -pl visibility-error-email`
WITHOUT `-am`. Without -am, visibility-commons:1.0 is resolved from ~/.m2, and its INSTALLED parent
pom ~/.m2/repository/com/inttra/mercury/visibility/1.0/visibility-1.0.pom (last installed 2026-07-24)
still carries <mercury.commons.version>1.0.27-SNAPSHOT</mercury.commons.version>.
With `-am` it correctly shows commons/cloud-sdk-api/cloud-sdk-aws = 1.0.33-SNAPSHOT.
GENERAL LESSON FOR THIS REPO: ALWAYS pass -am to dependency:tree / help:effective-pom, otherwise you
read stale installed poms. The Jenkins job already uses --also-make so CI was never affected.
Re-ran the whole §7.1 verification with -am: 4 lambdas have NO jna; all 7 other modules still resolve
jetty-setuid-jna:2.0.3 -> jna-jpms:5.14.0. Conclusion unchanged.

--- Q2: how did the s3-archiver IT survive a full build? ---
IT IS NEVER EXECUTED - not locally, not in CI.
Before yesterday: visibility/pom.xml log4j.version=2.23.1 AND s3-archiver hardcoded log4j-core 2.23.1
-> matched, no problem. Commit 08a0c83d41 bumped the property to 2.25.5, leaving log4j-core 2.23.1
against log4j-api 2.25.5 -> NoSuchMethodError ServiceLoaderUtil.loadServices.
Yesterday's documented local command (2026-08-31 doc line 199) was `mvn -pl visibility -amd clean
package` - failsafe binds to integration-test/verify, both AFTER package.
Jenkins job (supplied by user) is also package-only:
  mvn -ntp package sonar:sonar -P mercury-commons,sonar ... -pl ${app_dir} --also-make
TIMELINE PROOF: PR #1226 merged 2026-09-01 07:18 UTC; Jenkins built VisibilityS3Archiver-26.09.002 at
2026-09-01 09:02 UTC (workspace epoch stamp 1788253326) - i.e. 1h44m AFTER the bump - and SUCCEEDED.
So CI ran the broken combination and passed because it never runs the IT.
NOTE: log4j-core is <scope>test</scope> in s3-archiver -> the fix has ZERO effect on the deployed
artifact; it only repairs the IT.
FOLLOW-UP TO RAISE: CI should run `verify` so DynamoDB-Local ITs gate the build.

--- Q3: origin + fix versions of the jsoup / jackson HIGHs ---
jsoup 1.17.2  <- TRANSITIVE from commons 1.0.33-SNAPSHOT. Not declared anywhere in visibility.
                 Owned by mercury-services-commons. Fix requires a bump there, or a
                 dependencyManagement pin in visibility/pom.xml.
jackson-databind 2.22.0 <- DECLARED in visibility/visibility-commons/pom.xml:51-54 as
                 ${jackson.version}, set in visibility/pom.xml:36. WE own this one.
CVE-2026-75140 (jsoup) HIGH, CVSSv4 8.7, CWE-770: XmlTreeBuilder copies the whole inherited namespace
  map per start element -> quadratic memory -> OOM. Affects jsoup THROUGH 1.23.2. Fix commit 862ba2f,
  PR jhy/jsoup#2556. FIXED IN jsoup 1.23.3  <-- clean upgrade available, clears a HIGH.
CVE-2026-71497 (jsoup) MEDIUM XSS - same upgrade.
CVE-2026-68497 (jackson-databind) HIGH, CVSSv4 8.7, CWE-770: missing StreamReadConstraints number-len
  limit on XMLGregorianCalendar/Duration. PR FasterXML/jackson-databind#6127. Confirmed fixed in 3.1.6;
  NO published 2.22.x backport as of 2026-09-01.
jackson 2.22.1 exists and fixes CVE-2026-54515 / 59889 / 77310 (MEDIUMs) but NOT the HIGH.
RECOMMENDATION: do the jsoup bump first - it is the only one that actually reduces the HIGH count.

--- Q4: was copying the 12.2.2 data dir into 13.0.0 wrong / suppressions file invalid? ---
NO, the copy is harmless and the suppression file IS valid.
dependency-check-current -> symlink -> dependency-check-13.0.0.
12.2.2/data last refreshed 2026-08-31 19:48 (publishedSuppressions.xml 84,781 B).
13.0.0/data after copy + first run: 2026-09-01 15:16, publishedSuppressions.xml 85,038 B,
  *.properties grew 56 -> 59 bytes (rewritten under the new version marker),
  odc.mv.db 249,405,440 -> 249,643,008 B. No schema-mismatch error; scans run normally.
Functional proof it is valid: renaming it flips jna 0 -> 9 vulns and back (Q5).
THE REAL CAUSE of the jackson/jsoup difference is the 12.2.2 -> 13.0.0 UPGRADE, not the data copy:
  [WARN] Sonatype OSS Index Analyzer disabled due to missing credentials. Authentication with token
         is now required, and OSS Index is migrating to Sonatype Guide.
Both jackson CVE-2026-68497 and both jsoup CVEs are (OSSINDEX)-sourced, not NVD. Local JSON shows
vuln sources = ['NVD'] only and 0 occurrences of "OSSINDEX" in the HTML. Jenkins reports are ALSO
13.0.0 but contain 25-41 OSSINDEX hits each -> CI HAS AN OSS INDEX TOKEN, the workstation does not.
Under 12.2.2 OSS Index worked anonymously, which is why the user's earlier local scan showed
jackson+jsoup. So: three HIGHs, two data sources, each disabled in a different place.
NOTE: dependency-check-maven is COMMENTED OUT in the root pom - CI runs the DC CLI as its own step and
feeds Sonar via -Dsonar.dependencyCheck.htmlReportPath.

--- Q5: rename the suppression file and confirm the jna HIGH appears ---
DONE, in place, on a full reconstructed PRE-FIX s3-archiver package (222 jars = 220 + jna-jpms +
jetty-setuid-jna), with try/finally to guarantee restore.
  file present                     -> jna 0 vulns
  --disableHostedSuppressions only -> jna 0 vulns (flag stops REFRESH, not USE)
  file renamed to .DISABLED        -> jna {'HIGH': 4, 'MEDIUM': 5} = 9, CVE-2009-2476/2689/2475/2716...
  restored                         -> jna 0 vulns  (verified by re-scan)
EXACT match for Jenkins.
GOTCHA: while the real file is renamed away, DC writes a FRESH BUNDLED snapshot (82,965 B) into the
data dir. You must delete that and rename your original (85,038 B) back - a plain Rename-Item back
fails with "Cannot create a file when that file already exists". Handled and restored.

--- Doc changes ---
New/rewritten: §2.1 (stale-pom trap), §5 fully restructured into 5.1-5.5 with a 3-source summary
table, §6.3 expanded with the CI job + timeline, §7.1 re-verified with -am, §7.5 caveat rewritten,
new §9 (the other two HIGHs), §10/§11 renumbered, §8 gained commands 3a, 10(c), 10a, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21.

 Q1 §2.1  commons 1.0.27-SNAPSHOT was a PROBE ARTIFACT. dependency:tree without -am resolves sibling
          modules from ~/.m2 using the stale installed visibility-1.0.pom (2026-07-24). With -am it
          is 1.0.33-SNAPSHOT. CI unaffected (Jenkins uses --also-make).
 Q2 §6.3  The s3-archiver IT is never executed anywhere. failsafe binds to integration-test/verify;
          both the local command (mvn -pl visibility -amd clean package) and the Jenkins job
          (mvn ... package sonar:sonar ... --also-make) stop at package. PR #1226 merged 09-01
          07:18 UTC, Jenkins built 26.09.002 at 09:02 UTC and went green with the broken combo.
 Q3 §9    jsoup 1.17.2 is TRANSITIVE from commons (owned by mercury-services-commons) —
          CVE-2026-75140 HIGH, fixed in jsoup 1.23.3. jackson-databind 2.22.0 is DECLARED by us in
          visibility-commons via ${jackson.version} (visibility/pom.xml:36) — CVE-2026-68497 HIGH,
          fixed only in 3.1.6, no 2.22.x backport as of 2026-09-01 (2.22.1 clears 3 MEDIUMs only).
          Recommendation: bump jsoup first, it is the only one that lowers the HIGH count.
 Q4 §5.2/5.3  The 12.2.2 -> 13.0.0 data-dir copy was HARMLESS (13.0.0 re-downloaded
          publishedSuppressions.xml 84,781 -> 85,038 B, rewrote the .properties marker, no schema
          error). The real cause of the jackson/jsoup discrepancy is the VERSION UPGRADE: DC 13
          requires a token for Sonatype OSS Index ("disabled due to missing credentials"). Both

             + 5 MEDIUM, CVE-2009-2476/2689/2475/2716) | restored -> 0.
          Note --disableHostedSuppressions stops the file being REFRESHED, not USED. Restore gotcha:
          DC writes a fresh bundled snapshot (82,965 B) while the real file is renamed away, so the

entries.summary: OSS Index auth in DC 13: token needs the sonatype_pat_ prefix OR a username, else silently disabled
entries.detail:
Question: how to pass the OSS Index token to the dependency-check CLI to clear
"[WARN] Sonatype OSS Index Analyzer disabled due to missing credentials."

FLAG: --ossIndexPassword <token>  (there is no --ossIndexToken; the token goes in the password slot)
PROPERTY: analyzer.ossindex.password  (+ analyzer.ossindex.user for legacy tokens)
FILE: -P / --propertyfile <file>

CRITICAL GATE (not documented in --help; read from OssIndexAnalyzer.prepareAnalyzer() bytecode via
javap -p -c on dependency-check-core-13.0.0.jar):

  if (password.isEmpty() || (user.isEmpty() && !password.startsWith("sonatype_pat_")))
        -> LOG.warn("disabled due to missing credentials"); setEnabled(false);

So a password ALONE is not enough. The analyzer enables only when either:
  (a) the password starts with the literal prefix "sonatype_pat_" (Sonatype Guide PAT, no username
      required), or
  (b) BOTH analyzer.ossindex.user AND analyzer.ossindex.password are set (legacy OSS Index token;
      also logs a deprecation warning - legacy tokens must be replaced before 2026-12-31).

EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED with dummy values on a single-jar scan:
  password unset                       -> "disabled due to missing credentials"
  password=DUMMY_TOKEN, no user        -> STILL "disabled due to missing credentials" (no prefix)
  password=sonatype_pat_DUMMY, no user -> ENABLED; runs, then "invalid credentials" (exit 14)
  user + legacy password               -> ENABLED; runs, plus migration deprecation warning
The message changing from "missing credentials" to "invalid credentials" is the signal that the
credential was picked up.

OTHER VERIFIED FACTS:
- DC itself warns against the CLI flag: "[WARN] ossIndexPassword used on the command line, consider
  moving the password to a properties file using the key `analyzer.ossindex.password` and using the
  --propertyfile argument instead". This corroborates the earlier NVD-key hygiene advice - inline
  secrets are readable via Get-CimInstance Win32_Process and land in shell history.
- Default URL on 13.0.0 is already https://api.guide.sonatype.com (from the bundled
  dependencycheck.properties) - do NOT override --ossIndexUrl.
- OSS Index auth/remote failure is FATAL by default (exit 14). --ossIndexRemoteErrorWarnOnly true
  returns exit 0 (verified).
- Sonatype Guide free accounts are credit-metered per component report, unlike the old anonymous
  OSS Index. Preserve the DC data dir between runs (the OSS Index cache lives there) and consider
  analyzer.ossindex.cache.validforhours=168 locally. Argues for OSS Index on a scheduled CI job
  rather than every commit.

Documented in visibility/docs/2026-09-01-visibility-lambda-owasp.md as new section 5.2.1 plus
commands 22 / 22a / 22b in section 8. This closes the loop on the 5.2 diagnosis (CI has a token,
the workstation does not).

~/.dependency-check/dc.properties, passed via --propertyfile). Command:

  dependency-check.bat --project "VisibilityS3Archiver" \
    --scan  visibility\visibility-s3-archiver\target\visibility-s3-archiver-1.0-deployment_package.zip \
    --propertyfile $props --out owasp-reports\verify-s3-archiver \
    --format HTML --format JSON --ossIndexRemoteErrorWarnOnly true

  [INFO] Skipping the NVD API Update as it was completed within the last 240 minutes
  [INFO] Finished Sonatype OSS Index Analyzer (7 seconds)
  [INFO] Analysis Complete (37 seconds)     exit 0

RESULTS
  OSSINDEX mentions : 0 -> 25      (token accepted, analyzer actually ran)
  jna-jpms mentions : 0            (fix holds - artifact absent, not merely suppressed)
  jetty-setuid      : 0
  severity counts   : {'MEDIUM': 10, 'HIGH': 2}
  vuln sources      : {'OSSINDEX': 8, 'NVD': 4}

  HIGH OSSINDEX CVE-2026-68497  jackson-databind-2.22.0.jar
  HIGH OSSINDEX CVE-2026-75140  jsoup-1.17.2.jar

CONCLUSIONS NOW EVIDENCE-BACKED (previously inferred):
 1. The jna-jpms HIGH is genuinely gone from the lambda package.
 2. The only remaining HIGHs are exactly the two under the 2-week release exception, and their CVE
    ids match section 9 of the document precisely.
 3. Both are OSSINDEX-sourced -> confirms the section 5.2 diagnosis (missing OSS Index credential
    was the cause of the local-vs-Jenkins disagreement, NOT the data-dir copy or a bad suppression
    file).
 4. 4 NVD findings vs 8 OSS Index findings in a single package: a token-less local scan was blind to
    roughly two-thirds of the vulnerabilities.
 5. The "Skipping the NVD API Update ... within the last 240 minutes" line directly confirms the
    nvd.api.check.validforhours=4 behaviour documented in section 5.2.2.
